# Runbook — Job archive / un-archive (`job_archive`) (a press that never moves, a partial, a refused restore) (Successor-Remediation, Op Stds §43)

>   - Field-ops sync — portal job/hours/materials/equipment/incidents to Smartsheet → The archive pass relocates a closed job's six containers (and brings them back) → “An un-archive refuses — a folder already holds the job's name in the live tree.”

A §43 successor-remediation entry, written for the **Successor-Operator**: a trained operator who
runs Claude Code and reads Smartsheet rows, portal screens and alert emails, but does **not** read
code. The §42 code-reader rationale lives in the module docstring of `field_ops/job_archive.py`
(the two-call Smartsheet sequence, the inverted order per direction, the resume-by-id probe) and in
`field_ops/fieldops_sync.py::_archive_pass` (the queue that retries). Companions:
[project_closure.md](project_closure.md) (what closing a job does *besides* archiving),
[fieldops_sync.md](fieldops_sync.md) (the daemon this pass runs inside),
[hours_log_sync.md](hours_log_sync.md) (the standing trackers that ride along inside the folders).

## What archiving actually is

Pressing **Archive** on a job in the portal **records intent** — it moves nothing. The Mac-side
pass picks the job off its own queue on the next `fieldops-sync` cycle and relocates **six
containers**, then reports back. That separation is deliberate: it is what lets the screen say
"Archiving…" honestly instead of claiming a job is filed the instant a flag flipped.

| # | System | What moves | Where it lands |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Smartsheet | the job's **Safety** folder | `ITS — Archive / <Job> / Safety` |
| 2 | Smartsheet | the job's **Progress** folder (the Hours Log, Equipment, Material List, Material Incidents and Material Receipts trackers are *inside* it) | `ITS — Archive / <Job> / Progress` |
| 3 | Smartsheet | the job's **Purchase Orders** folder | `ITS — Archive / <Job> / Purchase Orders` |
| 4 | Smartsheet | the job's **Subcontracts** folder | `ITS — Archive / <Job> / Subcontracts` |
| 5 | Box | the job's folder under the **safety** root | `ITS Archive / <Job> / Safety` |
| 6 | Box | the job's folder under the **progress** root | `ITS Archive / <Job> / Progress` |

**Six, not eleven.** In Box, the safety root is shared by purchase orders, RFQs, vendor quotes and
subcontracts — so moving the job's safety folder carries all of those with it. Everything is a
**move**: folder ids, sheet ids, permalinks and cell history are all preserved, and nothing is ever
deleted. `<Job>` is the project name with any invisible characters dropped and `/` turned into `-`.

**Nothing else moves.** Not the PO / RFQ / Estimate / Subcontract logs, not the WSR / WPR review
rows, not the job's row in `ITS_Active_Jobs` (it stays, marked Archived), not the customer's
`ITS DATA` project folder, not `ITS Photos`, and not a single portal record.

**One thing changes that is easy to miss:** a Smartsheet folder that moves into the Archive
workspace is readable by whoever that workspace is shared with, and no longer by whoever the source
workspace was shared with. Archiving is a permissions change as well as a filing change.

## The two switches, and the one that bites

- `field_ops.fieldops_sync.sync_enabled` — the whole daemon.
- `field_ops.fieldops_sync.archive_enabled` — this pass on its own.

Both live in `ITS_Config` under Workstream `field_ops`. **Read the rows for their current values —
never a document, including this one.** Pausing either is safe at any time and loses nothing (the
queue keeps every requested job until it is worked). Turning one **on** is a capability activation:
read the row's full Description first and confirm with Seth.

> **The both-rule (Op Stds §44).** Tier-2 self-repair is allowed only for a fault that is
> **documented AND low-capability-class**. Anything **novel or high-class** escalates. The four
> fixed high-class categories are the **External Send Gate**, **secrets / auth**, **doctrine**, and
> **code changes**.

> **Both directions have now been drilled live** (2026-08-10): archive → un-archive → archive on a
> real job, every container relocated, every folder id preserved through all three moves. What has
> *not* been exercised is the **live-folder collision refusal** in Symptom 6 — no restore has yet
> met a live folder that re-grew the job's name. Treat that one case as novel and co-resolve it
> with Seth; the ordinary directions are documented and Tier-2-eligible.

---

## Symptom 0 — a watchdog **Check X** alert: "Job archive(s) not progressing"

**What you see.** A WARN (or, on a stall that persists, CRITICAL) `ITS_Errors` row from Script
`scripts.watchdog` whose message begins **"Job archive(s) not progressing."** It names each job by
`job_id`, with its direction, state, attempt count and age.

**Read the message first — it tells you which symptom below you are in.** Check X reports two
different faults and they have different repairs:

| The message says | What it means | Go to |
|---|---|---|
| **`N STOPPED (partial/failed …)`** | The relocation ran and stopped part-way. **Terminal — it will never retry on its own.** | Symptom 2 (`partial`) or Symptom 3 (`failed`) |
| **`N STUCK in the queue past …`** | The request was raised and nothing ever picked it up. | Symptom 1 — and read the gate clause in the message, it usually names the cause outright |

The message also states the archive pass's gate: either **"LIKELY CAUSE: the archive pass is GATED
OFF"** (with the exact `ITS_Config` row) or **"The archive pass IS enabled, so the gate is not the
cause"**. Trust that line — it is read from the same accessor the daemon itself uses, so it cannot
disagree with what the daemon is doing.

**Why this check exists.** Until 2026-08-10 there was **no** detector for any of this. A job parked
at `requested` was invisible to every alerting surface, and the portal's own display of that state
is a *green* banner reading "Waiting for the office Mac to pick this up" — honest, reassuring, and
it never escalates. `JOB-000030` sat that way for hours and was found only because the operator
asked why the button had done nothing.

**Cadence.** Check X runs on the watchdog's **daily** tier, so expect up to a day between the stall
and the alert. Both faults are standing conditions that wait for a human anyway. Severity climbs on
a capped ladder — WARN each day, CRITICAL on the 3rd consecutive day and then at widening intervals
— so a long-ignored stall keeps re-notifying without flooding `ITS_Errors` with rows that cannot be
rotated away.

**Nothing to repair here.** Check X only observes; it never advances or retries an archive. The
repair is whichever symptom below the message points at.

## Symptom 1 — "I pressed Archive and nothing is happening"

**What you see.** The job's Archive card sits on **"Archiving… Waiting for the office Mac to pick
this up."** for far longer than a few minutes. No folder has moved in Smartsheet or Box. There is
no error anywhere — no `ITS_Errors` row, no Review-Queue row, no alert email.

**This is the 2026-08-10 incident**, and the silence is the whole point of it: a pass whose gate is
off does not run, does not log, and cannot report anything. The job is not lost — it is sitting in
the queue exactly as requested, waiting for something to service it.

**Since 2026-08-10 the silence is bounded:** watchdog **Check X** now raises this within a day (see
Symptom 0). It does not fix anything — it just means you no longer have to notice on your own.

**What the Successor-Operator checks, in this order:**

1. **The pass gate.** `ITS_Config` → `field_ops.fieldops_sync.archive_enabled`, Workstream
   `field_ops`. A dark pass is an intentional state, not a fault.
2. **The daemon gate.** `field_ops.fieldops_sync.sync_enabled` in the same sheet. With this off,
   *no* pass runs — hours and materials would have stopped mirroring too, which is the tell.
3. **The daemon itself.** `ITS_Daemon_Health` → the `fieldops_sync` row. Is `Last Run` fresh (the
   interval comes from `field_ops.fieldops_sync.poll_interval_seconds`; a couple of minutes is
   normal)? If the row is stale, the launchd job is not firing — `launchctl list | grep
   fieldops-sync`.
4. **The system kill switch.** `ITS_Config` → `system.state`. `PAUSED` or `MAINTENANCE` stops every
   daemon cleanly.
5. **`ITS_Errors`** for Script `field_ops.fieldops_sync`, code `fieldops_archive_fetch_auth_failed`
   (CRITICAL) or `fieldops_archive_fetch_failed` — the pass could not read its queue at all
   (Symptom 7).

**The Claude prompt.** *"The fieldops_sync archive pass is not picking up job `<job_id>`. Read the
`field_ops.fieldops_sync.archive_enabled` and `sync_enabled` rows in ITS_Config, the `fieldops_sync`
row in ITS_Daemon_Health, and any ITS_Errors rows with Script `field_ops.fieldops_sync` or
`job_archive` from the last day, and tell me which of the two switches or the daemon is the reason —
read-only, change nothing."*

**Repair.** If a gate is off and it should be on, that is a capability activation — **escalate**.
If the daemon is simply not running, reloading the launchd job (`scripts/launchd/install.sh load
org.solutionsmith.its.fieldops-sync`) is low-class, and the queued job is picked up on the next
cycle with **no re-press needed** — nothing was lost.

**A browser gotcha, not a fault.** The Archive card stops refreshing itself after about ten
minutes, while still saying "This page updates itself". Reload the page before believing a stale
"Archiving…".

## Symptom 2 — "Partly archived — 4 of 6 folders moved" — THIS DOES NOT RETRY

**What you see.** A red banner reading **"Partly archived — N of 6 folders moved"**, a list headed
*"These did not move yet"*, and a **Try again** button.

**Say the important part first: nothing will resume this on its own.** The daemon's queue serves
only jobs whose archive is still `requested` or `in_progress`. A `partial` result is *terminal* for
the daemon — the job leaves the queue the moment it is reported. **The relocation resumes only when
a human presses "Try again".** The banner says so, and it is telling the truth. (An earlier version
of that panel said the system retries automatically; it does not, and that copy was corrected.)

Nothing is damaged in the meantime. Every container that did move is fully moved, and every step is
safe to repeat: a re-run finds the moved ones already gone and reports "nothing to move" for them,
then retries only the ones that failed.

**Reading *which* container is stuck.** The panel lists the folder labels — and here is the trap:
**"Safety" and "Progress" each appear twice**, once for Smartsheet and once for Box, with no system
shown. The six are always reported in the same fixed order — Safety, Progress, Purchase Orders,
Subcontracts (all Smartsheet), then Safety, Progress (Box) — so the *last* Safety/Progress in the
list are the Box ones. Do not rely on counting: the authoritative answer is in `ITS_Errors`.

**Where the real name is.** `ITS_Errors` → Script **`job_archive`**, Error code
**`archive_container_failed`**. Each WARN names the job, the system and the container, e.g.
`archive container FAILED for job_id='JOB-000017': box/Safety (box:safety)` — plus the underlying
error. One WARN per failed container per attempt.

**What the Successor-Operator checks:**

1. The `archive_container_failed` WARNs for this job — how many, which system, what error.
2. Whether the cause is one of the named ones below (a Box root, a permissions shortfall, a live
   folder collision) or a plain transient (a Smartsheet or Box 5xx, a timeout).
3. `ITS_Daemon_Health` → the `fieldops_sync` row: a stopped archive turns that cycle **DEGRADED**
   and writes `— N archive(s) STOPPED, will not resume without a re-press` into `Error Summary`.

**Repair (Tier-2, low-class).** For a plain transient: press **Try again** in the portal. That
re-raises the request and resets the attempt counter; the next cycle retries only the stuck
containers. Two re-presses that both stop in the same place is not a transient — stop pressing and
work the specific cause below or escalate.

**Never drag the folders by hand** to "help it along". The pass finds a container by name in its
live location; a folder you have already moved is invisible to it, and a live folder wearing the
wrong name is invisible to every other part of ITS that files into it — which is how a job ends up
with two folders and its filings split across them.

## Symptom 3 — "Nothing moved" (a `failed` archive)

**What you see.** The same red card, reading **"Nothing moved."**, with all six containers listed
as stuck.

Same rule as Symptom 2: **terminal, and it waits for "Try again".** The difference is diagnostic —
all six failing at once points at something common to all of them rather than at one container:

- the Smartsheet identity lost ADMIN on a workspace (Symptom 5 — but that normally skips the pass
  *before* it starts, so seeing it here means the shortfall appeared mid-pass);
- Smartsheet or Box is broadly unreachable (check the circuit breaker and `ITS_Errors` for the
  cycle);
- the job's folder key is empty — `ITS_Errors` Script `job_archive`, code
  `archive_folder_key_missing`. That should be impossible (the portal stamps it at request time) —
  **escalate**;
- the queued direction is neither `archive` nor `unarchive` — code `archive_direction_unknown`. The
  pass refuses to guess rather than run the wrong direction and report six false successes.
  **Escalate.**

## Symptom 4 — exactly the two **Box** folders failed (4 of 6)

**What you see.** A `partial` at 4 of 6, and the two stuck entries are the *last* Safety and
Progress in the list. The `archive_container_failed` WARNs name `box/Safety` and `box/Progress`,
with a message about a **Box root** being unset.

**What it means.** Each system works out its own destination independently, on purpose: a Box
problem must not strand the four healthy Smartsheet folders. The Box destination is an `ITS_Config`
row — `field_ops.box.archive_root_folder_id`, Workstream `field_ops` — and when it is empty the
pass **refuses** rather than treating an unreadable tree as an empty one. That refusal is the
feature: without it, "no folder found" would look identical to "nothing to move" and the job would
be reported archived while the documents sat where they were.

A single Box container failing instead of both points at that workstream's **source** root:
`safety_reports.box.portal_root_folder_id` or `progress_reports.box.portal_root_folder_id`.

**What the Successor-Operator checks.** Read those three rows in `ITS_Config` and report whether
each is non-empty. That is the whole Tier-2 action.

**Repair — escalate.** The value is a Box folder id produced by a Developer-Operator tool
(`scripts/migrations/build_box_roots.py`); a *wrong* id does not fail, it quietly files a
customer's documents into the wrong tree. Setting or correcting it is Seth's. Once it is right,
press **Try again** — the four already-archived Smartsheet folders report "nothing to move" and only
the two Box folders are retried.

## Symptom 5 — every archive is waiting, and the whole pass is skipping

**What you see.** Nothing moves for *any* queued job, and `ITS_Errors` carries a WARN with Script
**`job_archive`** and code **`archive_preflight_not_admin`** (or `archive_preflight_unreadable`),
naming a workspace id.

**What it means.** Before touching anything, the pass checks that the ITS Smartsheet identity holds
**ADMIN** on all five workspaces a move touches (Archive, Safety Portal, Progress Reporting,
Purchase Orders, Subcontracts). Without ADMIN, a folder move is refused by Smartsheet — and it
would be refused *partway through*, leaving jobs half-relocated for no reason other than a sharing
gap. So the pass **skips loudly and moves nothing**. The cycle is marked DEGRADED.

**This is the good failure.** Because nothing was attempted, no job is reported `partial` or
`failed` — every queued job stays on the queue, and they all proceed on the first cycle after the
share is fixed. **No re-press is needed.**

**What the Successor-Operator checks.** Read the WARN and note which workspace id is deficient and
what level it reports. Confirm in Smartsheet that the ITS identity appears on that workspace's
sharing list.

**Repair — escalate.** Workspace sharing is approval authority in ITS (§46) and the token's identity
is auth territory; both are fixed high-class. Report the workspace and the level you saw.

**Box is deliberately not pre-flighted.** It has no equivalent thing to probe, and its one
pre-flightable fault (an unset root, Symptom 4) already fails before any write — so skipping the
whole pass for it would strand the four healthy Smartsheet containers as well.

## Symptom 6 — an un-archive refuses: "folder … already holds that name in the live tree"

**What you see.** A `partial` or `failed` **un-archive**, with an `archive_container_failed` WARN
whose message says a folder already holds the job's name in the live tree and that neither system
can merge two folders.

**What it means, in plain terms.** The job was archived and then *written to* — a new safety
submission, a PO, an hours entry. Every filing path in ITS creates the job's folder if it cannot
find one, so the live tree grew a fresh `<Job>` folder beside the archived copy. Bringing the
archived one home would mean fusing two folders, and neither Smartsheet nor Box has a merge
operation. The pass refuses **loudly** instead of silently picking one. That refusal is correct.

**What the Successor-Operator checks.** In the workstream named by the WARN, look for two homes for
the same job: the live `<Job>` folder (recently created, probably nearly empty) and
`ITS — Archive / <Job> / <Workstream>` (or `ITS Archive / <Job> / …` in Box). Note what is in each.
**Change nothing.**

**Repair — escalate.** Reconciling two folders is hand work in two external systems with no undo,
and it requires deciding which sheets are canonical. Not Tier-2.

**Two more un-archive facts worth knowing before you touch one:**

- **The restore direction HAS been drilled live** (2026-08-10, issue #42) — archive → un-archive →
  archive, all containers, folder ids preserved throughout. The one branch still unexercised is the
  live-folder collision below; that specific case is novel → co-resolve with Seth.
- **"Try again" after a failed un-archive presses *Archive*, not un-archive.** The button on the
  red card always raises an archive request, and the confirmation modal it opens says so — read it.
  The result is recoverable, not harmful: the job goes back to fully archived, and the **Un-archive**
  button reappears once it reads Archived again. But it is not "resume the restore", and pressing it
  without reading the modal is how an operator convinces themselves the system is fighting them.

## Symptom 7 — "the archive queue could not be read"

**Evidence.** `ITS_Errors`, Script `field_ops.fieldops_sync`:

- **`fieldops_archive_fetch_auth_failed` (CRITICAL)** — the portal rejected the field-ops bearer
  token (401). No job was relocated this cycle; nothing is lost, everything stays queued.
  **Secrets / auth → escalate.** The Successor-Operator does not rotate tokens.
- **`fieldops_archive_fetch_failed` (ERROR)** — a transport blip reaching the portal. The queue
  re-serves next cycle; **self-heals**, no action unless it persists.

## Symptom 8 — "the folders moved but the portal still shows it running"

**Evidence.** `ITS_Errors`, Script `field_ops.fieldops_sync`, code
**`fieldops_archive_progress_failed`** (WARN).

The relocations already happened; only the report back to the portal failed. Nothing is lost —
the queue re-serves the job next cycle, every container reports "nothing to move", and the same
result is posted again. **Self-heals; no action.** That is exactly why it is a WARN and not a
CRITICAL.

A sibling, **`fieldops_archive_progress_skipped`** (WARN), means the operator changed the request
(or it already completed) while the pass was working — also not a fault.

## Symptom 9 — a stray empty folder in the Archive

**Evidence.** `ITS_Errors`, Script `job_archive`, code **`archive_job_folder_duplicate`** (WARN),
naming a folder id.

Two creators raced and Smartsheet allowed both (it does not enforce unique folder names). The
archive used the first one; the other is an **empty orphan**.

**Nothing to do.** It is harmless: the archive resolves its destination by find-or-create, so a
later archive of the same job reuses the folder it already picked and never touches the orphan.
ITS deliberately has no delete primitive for archive containers — the relocation code is
move-only by design, so a destructive "clean it up" path cannot be written. If the folder is
*not* empty, that is a different problem: leave it alone and escalate.

## What "healthy" looks like

- The Archive card moves **"Archiving…" → "Archived. All 6 folders are filed under
  `ITS — Archive / <Job>`"** within a cycle or two of the press.
- `ITS — Archive / <Job>/` holds four folders named Safety, Progress, Purchase Orders, Subcontracts;
  `ITS Archive / <Job>/` in Box holds two named Safety and Progress.
- The job's row in `ITS_Active_Jobs` is still there, marked Archived.
- `ITS_Daemon_Health` → `fieldops_sync` is OK, and the cycle summary line reads
  `archive complete=1 partial=0 failed=0 capped=0 errors=0`.
- No `job_archive` rows in `ITS_Errors`.
- Watchdog **Check X** reports `Job archives healthy: no archives in flight` (or `N archive(s) in
  flight, all within 0:30:00` while one is legitimately mid-relocation).

A note on the retry cap: the code stops auto-retrying a job after `MAX_ARCHIVE_ATTEMPTS` (20)
attempts, but in practice a job never gets near it — a `partial` or `failed` leaves the queue on the
first attempt, and a re-press resets the counter. If you ever see the pass report `capped=…`,
something is behaving in a way this runbook does not describe: **escalate**.

## Escalate to Seth (Tier 3) when

State it in what you *saw*, not what you think it is:

- **Turning either gate on** (`archive_enabled`, `sync_enabled`) — a capability activation. Pausing
  either is always safe and is yours.
- **`field_ops.box.archive_root_folder_id` is empty or you believe it is wrong** — a wrong folder id
  files documents into the wrong tree without failing.
- **`archive_preflight_not_admin` / `archive_preflight_unreadable`** — workspace sharing and the
  token identity are §46 / auth territory.
- **`fieldops_archive_fetch_auth_failed`** — a rejected token. Secrets / auth, always.
- **The live-folder collision in Symptom 6** — a restore refusing because the live tree re-grew the
  job's name. Both directions are drilled (2026-08-10, issue #42), but this branch has never fired
  against real data, and its repair means deciding which of two same-named trees is canonical.
- **`archive_folder_key_missing` or `archive_direction_unknown`** — both are "this should be
  impossible" signals from the code, not operating conditions.
- **The same container fails twice through "Try again"** with no cause named above.
- **Anything that would move a surface this pass does not touch** — the flat logs, the review rows,
  `ITS_Active_Jobs`, `ITS DATA`, `ITS Photos`. Extending what archival covers is a §51 doctrine
  question, not an operational tweak.
